content:
If one supplier's plans come to fruition, some memory chips for Apple devices will be manufactured in the United States for the first time.

The latest report indicates that Apple's memory supplier SK hynix is in discussions with Intel about using a chip factory Intel plans to build in Ohio...

Reuters reports that while details remain unclear at this stage, the Korean company produces RAM and flash memory chips for Apple devices.

Some processors for Apple devices are already made in the United States, but because foreign companies are restricted from using TSMC's most advanced processes, these processors can only be used in older models. However, since Apple uses industry-standard versions, DRAM or NAND flash memory chips are not affected by this restriction.

However, the report notes that the plan may face opposition from the South Korean government, as South Korea may have similar concerns as Taiwan about exporting chip manufacturing technology, even for older process nodes.

SK hynix said no decision has been made yet. Intel declined to comment on the report but confirmed it would continue to advance the development plans for the Ohio project.
